name: LED Bulb PAR38

verification.note: Read from the product having one load, which its group 1 controls, as on other one-load products.

steps.text: Turn off your light fixture and install the bulb.
Turn the light fixture on and leave it on.

notes: Don't connect the bulb to a dimmer; link it to Insteon remotes and switches to dim it.

If the switch or fixture is off, the bulb can't be controlled. If a wall switch controls the fixture, consider wiring it always on, for example by replacing it with an Insteon dimmer switch with its red load wire capped, then linking that switch to the bulb.

steps.text: With the controller in linking mode and the fixture on, unscrew the bulb for a moment if it's already in the socket.

notes: The bulb has no SET button and links only as a responder: it goes into linking mode each time it is powered up. Put the controller in linking mode first (press and hold its SET button until it beeps; on a multi-button controller, tap the button first).
Linking on power-up can be turned off with software (Disable Linking on Power-up); it is on by default.
For a scene, put the controller in multi-linking mode (hold its SET button until it beeps, then tap it), screw in each bulb one at a time, then tap the controller's SET button to finish.

verification.note: The LED Bulb PAR38 2674 Owner's Manual says the bulb double-beeps when it is linked or unlinked; the LED Bulb Developer Notes say the bulb has no SET button, status LED or beeper. The catalog follows the LED Bulb Developer Notes and gives no confirmation from the bulb.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
With the controller in linking mode and the fixture on, unscrew the bulb for a moment if it's already in the socket.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

The Insteon Developer's Guide (2009) lists Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 the group) as required of every device but i1 ones, and the Insteon Firmware Update i2CS Developer Notes give it to an i2CS device as an extended message with a checksum, from a sender that isn't in its ALL-Link database too. This profile's engine entries make every version of the product i2CS; no document names this product.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: With the controller in unlinking mode and the fixture on, unscrew the bulb for a moment.

notes: Put the controller in unlinking mode first: press and hold its SET button until it beeps (on a multi-button controller, tap the button first), then press and hold it again until it beeps.

verification.note: The LED Bulb PAR38 2674 Owner's Manual says the bulb double-beeps when it is linked or unlinked; the LED Bulb Developer Notes say the bulb has no SET button, status LED or beeper. The catalog follows the LED Bulb Developer Notes and gives no confirmation from the bulb.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a responder.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
With the controller in unlinking mode and the fixture on, unscrew the bulb for a moment.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset should clear them.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's unlinking steps and the standard Insteon command Start ALL-Linking; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Powers up on by default, and can be set to power up to its last state instead.
